## R Markdown Introduction

R markdown is a great way of producing a document which has both code and writing in it. Within R markdown you 
can write comments to the reader while creating executable code chunks all in the same space. This file
format seems great for reporting and commenting on code you want to show to a viewer.

## Narrative Paragraph

I have a decent amount of experience of with R markdown already, as I use it for all my assignments in my other class LIS 4761.
I find it to be an efficient way to code while reporting on my analysis finding so I think it's a great format to showcase findings.

## Executable R code chunks
```{r Summary Stats}
head(mtcars)
str(mtcars)
summary(mtcars)
```

```{r mtcars Plot}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg))+
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Weight vs. MPG",
  x = "Weight (per 1000 lbs)",
  y = "Miles per Gallon"
  )
```

## Concluding Reflection

In conclusion, I find R markdown to be a fantastic reporting tool for those who want to conduct analysis and explain their findings.
I find it to have a very organized and easy to understand structure, making it a great way of communicating findings to a broad audience.
One R markdown aspect I particularly enjoyed was its swappable view option from "source" to "visual", and I use this feature often when doing assignments in my other class. In comparison to plain reports on MS word or any other application, I definitely prefer R markdown since it makes
embedding code and placing commentary so easy.
